St. Dovmont-Timothy of Pskov

St. Dovmont of Pskov · St. Timothy of Pskov · Dovmont-Timothy · Dovmont · St. Daumantas of Pskov

Period

Introduction

St. Dovmont took the Christian name Timothy, ruled Pskov and was remembered for defending the city and caring for its people.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeathCommemoration and legacyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Died in 1299 after his final defense of Pskov; buried in Trinity cathedral

Read circumstances and sources

Background

St. Dovmont was a Lithuanian prince who reached Pskov as a refugee in 1265. The OCA says that he accepted baptism with the name Timothy and was soon chosen as the city’s prince. Pskov became the principal setting of his Christian life.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Opening two paragraphs

Life and notable events

The received life links his public service with almsgiving, hospitality, support for churches and defense against military attacks. It credits him with a long period of cooperation with the city council and with strengthening Pskov’s defenses. His marriage joined him to a Russian princely family; his wife later became the nun St. Martha of Pskov.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Justice and charity; public defense; reference to his wife

Death

After defending the city in 1299, he died later that year and was buried in Pskov’s Trinity cathedral. The account does not describe his death as an execution or martyrdom.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Final battle and burial

Commemoration and legacy

The OCA commemorates him on May 20 and records his sword and later intercession narratives. These are received hagiography.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Veneration, sword and commemoration heading
